messages.author: d0a6c4e0144772a5
messages.subject: Extracting mean annual temperatures
parts:
Hi all,

I am using the micro_global dataset and interested in microniche values.

I was wondering if there is a streamline way to calculate the mean temperature values for a site with a variable like TALOC (air temperature at local height). Ideally I am looking for the mean annual or monthly annual temperature from this site. Is there a built in function to do this without extracting the hourly info for everyday and summing it through a loop?

 

Currently my code looks like:

loc <- c(-89.944, 15.083)

dstart <- "01/05/2009"

dfinish <-"01/05/2009"

micro <- micro_ncep(loc = loc, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish)

 

Thank you in advance for any help!

Sarah

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Extracting mean annual temperatures
parts:
Hi Sarah,

This is more of an R than an NicheMapR question, but here's how you can do it e.g. per day or per month:

loc <- c(-89.944, 15.083)

dstart <- "01/01/2008"

dfinish <-"31/12/2009"
micro <- micro_ncep(loc = loc, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish)

dates <- micro$dates
metout <- as.data.frame(micro$metout)

# daily
taloc.max.daily <- aggregate(metout$TALOC, by=list(format(dates, "%d/%m/%Y")), FUN = max) # aggregate by day
colnames(taloc.max.daily) <- c('date', 'max.taloc') # change default column names from aggregate
taloc.max.daily$date <- as.POSIXct(taloc.max.daily$date, format = '%d/%m/%Y') # change dates from character back to date format
taloc.max.daily <- taloc.max.daily[order(taloc.max.daily$date), ] # sort by date (the order got changed by aggregate)
plot(taloc.max.daily)

#monthly
taloc.max.monthly <- aggregate(metout$TALOC, by=list(format(dates, "%m/%Y")), FUN = max)
colnames(taloc.max.monthly) <- c('date', 'max.taloc')
taloc.max.monthly$date <- paste0('15/', taloc.max.monthly$date) # extra step compared to above - pasting the middle day of each month to the date string
taloc.max.monthly$date <- as.POSIXct(taloc.max.monthly$date, format = '%d/%m/%Y')
taloc.max.monthly <- taloc.max.monthly[order(taloc.max.monthly$date), ]
plot(taloc.max.monthly)

All the best,
Mike
